method: Node-driven manual renders (same method as reports/perf-before.json: in-page rAF does not fire reliably headless, so each iteration positions the camera and calls renderer.render once, timed from Node. SwiftShader render time is a LOWER BOUND, never quoted as game performance — it measures the CPU software rasterizer, not the game logic or real-GPU frame time.

perf_avenue_onfoot.camera: on foot at (0, 0.2, -20) looking down Corso Azzurra to (0, 0.5, 20), viewport 1280x720

avenue_calls.note: +52 calls are the walkers visible on the avenue (7 walkers x 7 meshes); triangles fell 547504 -> 538040 (-1.7%). ms/frame avg 6215.6 -> 6827.4 (+9.8%) and median 6569 -> 7000 (+6.6%) is inside SwiftShader run-to-run noise on shared CPU (the BEFORE run itself ranged 25..8576 ms); the render cost is the software rasterizer, not the game.

vs_before.verdict: All views under 600 draw calls (worst 488 street-car). Whole-city ortho 238, down from 255 — the crossing-skipped trees/benches and skipped lamps outweigh the 34 added walkers at city scale.
